Support vector machine / Linear classifier

Which side of the line?

A linear SVM learns a straight boundary between two reference classes. The sign of w · z + b determines the class. The margin shows how the training points constrain the boundary.

Loading model...

The existing 40-row dataset is synthetic teaching data. These reference classes explain the classifier; they do not diagnose diabetes.

The learned line and margin

Both axes use standardized features, z = (x - mean) / scale, with equal units. The gold segment is perpendicular to the decision boundary.

−1 circles+1 squaresInput diamondRings: support vectors

Solid line: score = 0. Dashed lines: score = −1 and +1. Shaded strip: margin, which contains portions of both classes.

How this decision was reached

A score of zero belongs to +1 by convention. The score is a signed decision value, not a probability. Being inside the margin does not create a third class.

What training learned

min ½ ||w||² + C sum ξi
subject to yi (w · zi + b) ≥ 1 − ξi
margin width = 2 / ||w||

Sequential minimal optimization solves the linear dual problem. Support vectors have nonzero dual multipliers, α. A finite C permits margin violations.
